sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026 [Glottolog ref 710158: 2025]. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: Unravelling their prehistory and classification. Berlin: Language Science Press (langsci 526). doi:10.5281/zenodo.18323007
sources.note: Nothing Rajong-specific. p.116: Rajong is one of 'several poorly described languages... In the absence of sufficient data... we place them... as isolates within West Central Flores'; p.163: 'Rajong [rjg] (very little data available)'. Only stress remark is areal (sec. 3.2.1.2, p.115): 'While penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages, words with penultimate schwa can have stress on other syllables.'

sources.note: Nothing on Rajong phonology (its sec. 5.1.1 phonology is Rembong-Wangka segment inventory only). pp.2-3: Rajong 6,000 speakers, Manggarai Timur, kampung Nunur ('Rajong kecil') and 'Razong besar'; Verheijen lexicostatistics Rajong-Manggarai 67%. p.9: Erb (1987) and Quaaden (2009) contain Rajong ritual/song texts. p.42 sec. 6.4: 'Kepo', Rajong and Kolor, have hardly been investigated at all'.
